title: Student words in their own field
statement: Put a student's words in a field of their own in the judge's input and ask about that field by name, never inside the question's wording.
detail: The lesson engine's two writing blocks that judge a student's words at play time put them in named fields of the judge's state: student_text in the debate, and claim, evidence and reasoning in the claim-evidence-reasoning paragraph; its open check does the same with student_text. Their questions name those fields, and the options the judge picks among are written in advance, never taken from the student's text. A guard on words aimed at the marker is asked beside each of these judgments.
against: No test compares this with putting the words inside the question, so the benefit is not measured.
